free_tier.stated: 5 GB for every Amazon customer. Unlimited full-resolution photo storage plus 5 GB of video for Amazon Prime members

per_object_cap.stated: 5 GB of video even on Prime; photos are unlimited. Paid plans exist above 5 GB

retention.stated: While the account and the Prime membership persist; photos are removed from the unlimited tier if Prime lapses

egress.terms: Downloads run through Amazon's CDN, effectively free and fast, but only for objects the account uploaded

tooling: unofficial and cookie-authenticated only: trevorhobenshield/amazon_photos in Python, entourloop/amazon-photo-uploader in Rust, and an MCP server. There is no OAuth and no API key, and every wrapper says cookies expire and must be refreshed by hand. No rclone backend
chaining: The classic unlimited-photos shape: if arbitrary image bytes are accepted, and they are because it is a photo service, then a photo-shaped payload is free across accounts. The 5 GB video cap is what stops it being a general drive, and the absence of an API stops it being a pipeline

limits.value: 5 GB of video total, even on Prime; photos are unlimited but must be photographs
cookie authentication with no OAuth or key flow, so the credential is a browser session that expires

identity_cost.detail: an Amazon account and a Prime membership. Prime is the price of admission, so unlimited is bundled and not free

reliability_note: Cookie-authenticated wrappers break on any change to Amazon's login flow; the MCP wrapper's own README calls it an unofficial API that may break. Photo-only means ingest may re-encode or reject non-image payloads

evidence.proved: '5 GB of free storage for all Amazon customers. Unlimited full-resolution photo storage, plus 5 GB of video storage, for Amazon Prime members'
'unlimited photo storage and 5 GB of video storage to Amazon Prime members in eight marketplaces'
a Python client with md5 deduplication that preserves directory structure on upload
'Amazon Photos has no OAuth or API key flow' 'Cookie auth is fragile'

price_per_tb_month: Bundled with Prime at about USD 139/yr; the unlimited photo tier has no standalone price
binding_note: The capacity is genuinely unlimited for photographs and the gate is the credential: a browser cookie with no OAuth flow, which expires and cannot be renewed programmatically. That makes it a manual-ingest target at any scale.
notes: Both seed records are folded in here: one called it qualifies-with-caveat on the unlimited photo tier, another called it a dead end because Prime is paid and the video cap is 5 GB. Both are correct; the verdict is qualifies-with-caveat because the unlimited half is real and the caveat is the cookie auth plus the paid membership.
